candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — laboratory and diagnostic-test interpretation
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret elevated 24-hour urinary protein as an abnormal but nonspecific finding requiring clinical correlation.

options.A: Any elevation in urine protein by itself proves nephrotic syndrome.
options.B: Urinary protein has no upper reference limit in healthy adults, so the result is expected.
options.C: An elevated urine protein result specifically diagnoses multiple myeloma without further evaluation.
options.D: Proteinuria is abnormal and warrants interpretation in clinical context because multiple renal and nonrenal conditions can increase urinary protein.

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories provides a reference interval for 24-hour urinary protein and describes increased protein excretion in multiple conditions. An elevated result is abnormal but does not independently establish nephrotic syndrome, multiple myeloma, or another single cause. Clinical context and appropriate follow-up are required.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Elevated 24-hour urine protein is abnormal and may occur in multiple conditions; the result is not disease-specific by itself.
candidate.source_version_date: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories test catalog; accessed 2026-08-16
candidate.stem: An adult's 24-hour urine collection shows total protein above the laboratory reference interval. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

warning: Technical candidate selection only. This file is not clinical audit evidence and does not establish PASS or FAIL.
